title: Differentiation
overview: Differentiate implicitly and parametrically, on top of product/quotient/chain rules, for curves not given simply as y = f(x). This guide turns the current syllabus outcomes into a connected revision sequence: learn the ideas, practise the method, then use the recall cards and checklist to diagnose what still needs work.
syllabusPoints: Differentiate eˣ, ln x, trigonometric functions and tan⁻¹x, including composite functions.
Use product, quotient and chain rules accurately.
Find tangents, normals, stationary points and rates of change.

definitions.definition: An equation connecting x and y without y isolated as a function of x.
Equations x=f(t), y=g(t) describing a curve through a parameter t.
A line perpendicular to the tangent at the point of contact.
A rule for differentiating a composite function by multiplying derivatives through its layers.

sections.title: Core derivatives and chain rule
content: Memorise d(eˣ)/dx=eˣ, d(ln x)/dx=1/x, d(sin x)/dx=cos x, d(cos x)/dx=−sin x, d(tan x)/dx=sec²x and d(tan⁻¹x)/dx=1/(1+x²). For f(g(x)), multiply f′(g(x)) by g′(x).
bullets: ln|u| differentiates to u′/u wherever u≠0.

sections.title: Products and quotients
content: For y=uv, y′=u′v+uv′. For y=u/v, y′=(vu′−uv′)/v². Label u and v first and simplify after differentiating, especially when a second derivative is required.
bullets: The quotient-rule numerator order is denominator×derivative of numerator minus numerator×derivative of denominator.
A product can sometimes be rewritten to use the chain rule more cleanly.

sections.title: Implicit differentiation
content: Differentiate every term with respect to x and attach dy/dx whenever a y-term is differentiated. Collect all dy/dx terms on one side and factor. Substitute the point only after obtaining a usable derivative expression.
bullets: For xy use the product rule: d(xy)/dx=y+x(dy/dx).

sections.title: Parametric differentiation
content: If x=f(t) and y=g(t), then dy/dx=(dy/dt)/(dx/dt), provided dx/dt≠0. For d²y/dx², differentiate dy/dx with respect to t and divide by dx/dt again.
bullets: Find the parameter value corresponding to the stated point.
Normal gradient is −1/(dy/dx) when the tangent gradient is non-zero.

examTips: Show the derivative formula before substituting numerical coordinates.
For stationary points, use the derivative sign or d²y/dx² to classify when asked.
Show the mathematical setup and exact working before the final rounded answer; unsupported calculator output may not earn method marks.
commonMistakes: Forgetting dy/dx when differentiating a y-term implicitly.
Stopping at d(dy/dx)/dt instead of dividing by dx/dt for d²y/dx².

quickRecall.question: How is dy/dx found from x=f(t), y=g(t)?
What happens when y² is differentiated implicitly?
What is the normal gradient?
quickRecall.answer: It is the negative reciprocal of the tangent gradient, when defined.

quickRecall.question: Why are radians essential for trig differentiation?
quickRecall.answer: The standard derivative formulae for sin x, cos x and tan x are valid without extra factors only in radians.
